근거 ❹ · 해석: 상실을 존중하는 한편, 애도 작업은 개인적 변화와 삶이 계속되기 위한 토대를 마련한다.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) costly — (B) fully developed — (C) captured
(A) costly — (B) unexploited — (C) preserved
(A) costly — (B) unexploited — (C) captured
(A) affordable — (B) fully developed — (C) preserved
(A) affordable — (B) unexploited — (C) captured
choice.ex: (A) costly (B) unexploited (C) captured 근거 ❷❹❺❻❼ 해설: (A) ❷ 삶의 재생산은 비싸고 점점 더 비싸진다, ❹~❻ 노동·에너지·작물이 차례로 비싸짐 → costly. affordable은 정반대. (B) ❶ 현금 교환의 섬 바깥의 값싼 만물, ❼ Frontiers(미개척 영역) → 아직 착취되지 않은 지역. fully developed(이미 개발된)는 섬 안쪽, 즉 이미 비싸진 곳이므로 반대. (C) ❼ can be seized / forcefully taken → captured(손에 넣다). preserved(보존되다)는 ‘값싼 것을 취한다’는 논지와 반대. 요약문 해석: 자본주의의 화폐 교환 구역 안에서 노동자·에너지·식량을 유지하는 것이 점점 더 (A) 비용이 많이 들게 되기 때문에, 그 체제는 새로운 값싼 노동과 자원을 (C) 손에 넣을 수 있는 (B) 아직 착취되지 않은 지역에 의존한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Capitalism is not a system where cash is everywhere but rather one in which islands of cash exchange exist within oceans of cheap — or potentially cheap — natures. ❷ Reproducing life within the cash nexus is expensive, and it grows more expensive over time. ❸ Workers’ wages can be frozen, even rolled back, but in the end inequality leads to crises of the kind we’ve recently seen bring about populist protests in the United States and the United Kingdom. ❹ Workers demand dignity, and their labor becomes expensive. ❺ Production processes burn through an island, and energy is no longer cheap. ❻ The climate changes, and crops can no longer grow as abundantly as they once did. ❼ Frontiers are so important in these processes because they offer places where the new cheap things can be seized — and the cheap work of humans and other natures can be forcefully taken.
choice.body: Because sustaining workers, energy, and food inside capitalism’s zones of money exchange grows ever more (A)________, the system depends on (B)________ areas where new cheap labor and resources can be (C)________.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) vanish — (B) harmony — (C) flourish
(A) vanish — (B) upheaval — (C) shrink
(A) last — (B) upheaval — (C) flourish
(A) last — (B) upheaval — (C) shrink
(A) last — (B) harmony — (C) shrink
choice.ex: (A) last (B) upheaval (C) shrink 근거 ❷❸❻ 해설: (A) ❷ 시간이 흐를수록 더 비싸진다 → 낮은 비용은 오래가지 않는다(do not last). ‘do not vanish(사라지지 않는다)’를 넣으면 값싼 상태가 유지된 다는 뜻이 되어 정반대. (B) ❸ 결국 불평등이 위기를 초래하고 포퓰리스트 시위를 낳았다 → upheaval(격변). harmony(조화)는 반대. (C) ❻ 작물이 예 전만큼 풍부하게 자라지 않는다 → shrink(줄어들다). flourish(번성하다)는 반대. 요약문 해석: 자본주의의 화폐 교환 구역 안에서 낮은 비용은 (A) 지속되지 않는다. 임금은 일정 기간만 억제될 수 있을 뿐 커지는 불공정이 결국 (B) 격변 을 촉발하며, 노동자들이 존엄성을 추구하고 수확량이 (C) 줄어들면서 새로운 값싼 공급원을 찾는 일이 시급해진다.
choice.psg: ❶ Capitalism is not a system where cash is everywhere but rather one in which islands of cash exchange exist within oceans of cheap — or potentially cheap — natures. ❷ Reproducing life within the cash nexus is expensive, and it grows more expensive over time. ❸ Workers’ wages can be frozen, even rolled back, but in the end inequality leads to crises of the kind we’ve recently seen bring about populist protests in the United States and the United Kingdom. ❹ Workers demand dignity, and their labor becomes expensive. ❺ Production processes burn through an island, and energy is no longer cheap. ❻ The climate changes, and crops can no longer grow as abundantly as they once did. ❼ Frontiers are so important in these processes because they offer places where the new cheap things can be seized — and the cheap work of humans and other natures can be forcefully taken.
choice.body: Within capitalism’s zones of money exchange, low costs do not (A)________: wages can be held down only for so long before growing unfairness sparks (B)________, and as workers seek dignity and harvests (C)________, the hunt for fresh cheap supplies becomes urgent.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Capitalism looks beyond its existing zones of money exchange for new sources of cheap labor.
Environmental change can turn something that used to be cheap into something pricier.
Holding wages down may delay serious trouble, but it cannot prevent such trouble indefinitely.
Keeping workers paid and fed within a money economy tends to cost more as time passes.
The recent populist protests in America and Britain were mainly caused by rising energy prices.
choice.ex: ❸에서 포퓰리스트 시위를 낳은 위기의 원인은 ‘불평등’이다. 에너지가 더 이상 값싸지 않게 된다는 내용(❺)은 별개의 과정으로 제시 될 뿐, 시위의 원인으로 연결되지 않는다(본문의 두 사실을 엮은 거짓 인과). ① 근거 ❶❼ — 자본주의는 새로운 값싼 노동력의 공급원을 찾아 기존의 화폐 교환 구역 너머를 바라본다. ② 근거 ❻ — 환경 변화는 예전에 값쌌던 것을 더 비싼 것으로 바꿀 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❸ — 임금을 억제하는 것은 심각한 문제를 늦출 수는 있지만, 그런 문제를 무기한 막을 수는 없다. ④ 근거 ❷❹ — 화폐 경제 안에서 노동자들에게 임금을 주고 먹을 것을 대는 일은 시간이 흐를수록 비용이 더 드는 경향이 있다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 최근 미국과 영국의 포퓰리스트 시위는 주로 에너지 가격 상승 때문에 일어났다.
choice.psg: ❶ Capitalism is not a system where cash is everywhere but rather one in which islands of cash exchange exist within oceans of cheap — or potentially cheap — natures. ❷ Reproducing life within the cash nexus is expensive, and it grows more expensive over time. ❸ Workers’ wages can be frozen, even rolled back, but in the end inequality leads to crises of the kind we’ve recently seen bring about populist protests in the United States and the United Kingdom. ❹ Workers demand dignity, and their labor becomes expensive. ❺ Production processes burn through an island, and energy is no longer cheap. ❻ The climate changes, and crops can no longer grow as abundantly as they once did. ❼ Frontiers are so important in these processes because they offer places where the new cheap things can be seized — and the cheap work of humans and other natures can be forcefully taken.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: spread the money economy evenly across every corner of the planet
use up the cheap resources within a zone of money exchange until they stop being cheap
create new supplies of cheap energy inside a market zone
set fire to a piece of land that is surrounded by the sea
force workers to move from one country to another
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 생산 과정이 섬을 다 태워 버린다 → 현금 교환 구역 안의 값싼 자원을 소진하여 더 이상 값싸지 않게 만든다 해설: ❶에서 ‘섬(island)’은 값싼 만물의 바다 안에 있는 ‘현금 교환의 섬’이다. burn through는 ‘다 태워 없애다 → 소진하다’이고, 같은 문장 뒤의 ‘에너지 는 더 이상 값싸지 않다’가 그 결과다. ‘바다로 둘러싸인 땅에 불을 지른다’는 문자 그대로의 해석, ‘값싼 에너지 공급원을 만든다’는 정반대, ‘화폐 경제를 지 구 구석구석에 퍼뜨린다’는 ❶에서 필자가 부정한 내용, ‘노동자 강제 이주’는 무관. ① 화폐 경제를 지구 구석구석에 고르게 퍼뜨린다 ② 화폐 교환 구역 안의 값싼 자원을 그것이 더 이상 값싸지 않을 때까지 다 써 버린다 ③ 시장 구역 안에 값싼 에너지의 새로운 공급원을 만들어 낸다 ④ 바다로 둘러싸인 땅에 불을 지른다 ⑤ 노동자들을 한 나라에서 다른 나라로 강제로 이주시킨다
choice.body: Workers demand dignity, and their labor becomes expensive. Production processes burn through an island, and energy is no longer cheap. The climate changes, and crops can no longer grow as abundantly as they once did.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) obligation — (B) offset — (C) equilibrium
(A) right — (B) offset — (C) equilibrium
(A) right — (B) offset — (C) disorder
(A) right — (B) deepen — (C) equilibrium
(A) obligation — (B) deepen — (C) disorder
choice.ex: (A) right (B) offset (C) equilibrium 근거 ❶❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❶ 친환경 선택을 착한 행위로 여겨 그렇게 할 자격이 있다고 느낀다 → 잘못 행동할 ‘권리(right)’를 얻었다고 믿음. obligation(의무)은 ‘해도 된 다’가 아니라 ‘해야 한다’라서 틀림. (B) ❹ compensate for this guilt → 죄책감을 상쇄하다(offset). deepen(깊게 하다)은 반대. (C) ❹ restore balance, ❺ re-establish the moral balance → 균형(equilibrium). disorder(무질서)는 반대. 요약문 해석: 친환경 구매는 사람들로 하여금 자신이 잘못 행동할 (A) 권리를 얻었다고 믿게 할 수 있는 반면, 과거에 환경에 끼친 해악을 떠올리는 것은 그 들이 추가적인 친환경 행동을 통해 (B) 상쇄하려고 하는 죄책감을 만들어 낸다. 이는 사람들이 자신의 도덕적 삶을 (C) 균형 상태로 유지하려고 애쓴다는 것을 보여 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing “eco-friendly” products, probably because they feel licensed to do so since they morally account the “eco-friendly” choice as a “good” deed. ❷ Moral licensing has also been observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment. ❸ When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of “eco-guilt.” ❹ People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance. ❺ In their search for such a balance, people are inclined to believe in “quick-fixes,” because they want to re-establish the moral balance and escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible. ❻ In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their evaluation of past environmentally burdening behaviors and future environmentally friendly behaviors. ❼ For instance, people are more likely to sign a petition addressing environmental damage after viewing evidence of human-caused environmental damage.
choice.body: A green purchase can leave people believing they have earned the (A)________ to misbehave, whereas recalling their past environmental harm produces guilt that they try to (B)________ through further eco-friendly acts — showing that people strive to keep their moral lives in (C)________.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) ignore — (B) reevaluate — (C) eager
(A) ignore — (B) forget — (C) reluctant
(A) modify — (B) forget — (C) eager
(A) modify — (B) reevaluate — (C) eager
(A) modify — (B) reevaluate — (C) reluctant
choice.ex: (A) modify (B) reevaluate (C) eager 근거 ❻❼ 해설: (A) ❻ change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies → 태도를 수정하다(modify). ignore(무시하다)로는 간극을 메울 수 없음. (B) ❻ change their evaluation of past … and future … behaviors → 재평가하다(reevaluate). forget(잊다)은 본문에 없는 내용. (C) ❼ 증거를 본 후 청원 서에 서명할 가능성이 더 높다 → 더 열성적인(eager). reluctant(꺼리는)는 반대. 요약문 해석: 사람들이 자신이 생각하는 것과 행하는 것 사이의 간극을 메우기 위해 태도를 (A) 수정하는 것처럼, 그들은 과거의 해로운 습관과 미래의 친 환경 행동을 (B) 재평가할 수 있는데, 이것이 인간이 유발한 훼손의 증거를 보는 것이 그들을 환경 운동을 지지하는 데 더 (C) 열성적으로 만드는 이유이 다.
choice.psg: ❶ Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing “eco-friendly” products, probably because they feel licensed to do so since they morally account the “eco-friendly” choice as a “good” deed. ❷ Moral licensing has also been observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment. ❸ When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of “eco-guilt.” ❹ People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance. ❺ In their search for such a balance, people are inclined to believe in “quick-fixes,” because they want to re-establish the moral balance and escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible. ❻ In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their evaluation of past environmentally burdening behaviors and future environmentally friendly behaviors. ❼ For instance, people are more likely to sign a petition addressing environmental damage after viewing evidence of human-caused environmental damage.
choice.body: Just as people (A)________ their attitudes to close the gap between what they think and what they do, they may (B)________ their past harmful habits and future green acts, which is why seeing proof of human-caused damage makes them more (C)________ to support environmental causes.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Guilt about the environment shapes behavior more strongly than the sense of moral permission does.
Seeing evidence of environmental damage caused by humans can push people to act on behalf of nature.
Buying products labeled as green does not necessarily make people behave more ethically.
Remembering one’s past harm to nature can give rise to an uncomfortable emotion.
People who carry guilt about the environment may try to make up for it through green behavior.
choice.ex: 본문은 도덕적 허가(❶❷)와 환경 죄책감(❸~❼)을 각각 설명할 뿐, 둘 중 어느 것이 행동에 더 강한 영향을 미치는지는 비교하지 않는 다(본문에 없는 비교). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 환경에 대한 죄책감은 도덕적 허가의 감각보다 행동을 더 강하게 형성한다. ② 근거 ❼ — 인간이 유발한 환경 훼손의 증거를 보는 것은 사람들이 자연을 위해 행동하도록 떠밀 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❶ — 친환경이라고 표시된 제품을 산다고 해서 반드시 사람들이 더 윤리적으로 행동하게 되는 것은 아니다. ④ 근거 ❸ — 자연에 끼친 자신의 과거 해악을 떠올리는 것은 불편한 감정을 불러일으킬 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 ❹ — 환경에 대한 죄책감을 지닌 사람들은 친환경 행동을 통해 그것을 만회하려 할 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing “eco-friendly” products, probably because they feel licensed to do so since they morally account the “eco-friendly” choice as a “good” deed. ❷ Moral licensing has also been observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment. ❸ When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of “eco-guilt.” ❹ People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance. ❺ In their search for such a balance, people are inclined to believe in “quick-fixes,” because they want to re-establish the moral balance and escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible. ❻ In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their evaluation of past environmentally burdening behaviors and future environmentally friendly behaviors. ❼ For instance, people are more likely to sign a petition addressing environmental damage after viewing evidence of human-caused environmental damage.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: prefer cheaper products over eco-friendly ones
commit to long-term changes that require serious personal sacrifice
expect new technology to solve every environmental problem soon
rely on tools that repair broken household items in a short time
trust in simple actions that relieve their guilt fast without demanding much real change
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: ‘임시방편’을 믿으려 한다 → 큰 노력 없이 죄책감을 빠르게 덜어 주는 손쉬운 행동에 기댄다 해설: 같은 문장의 이유절 ‘도덕적 균형을 재정립하고 가능한 한 빠르고 쉽게 죄책감에서 벗어나고 싶어 하기 때문’이 quick-fixes의 의미를 풀어 준다 → 빠르고 손쉽게 죄책감을 덜어 주는 행동. ‘가정용품 수리 도구’는 fix의 문자적 의미, ‘희생을 요구하는 장기적 변화’는 정반대, ‘기술이 모든 환경 문제를 해 결’은 범위 확대, ‘더 저렴한 제품 선호’는 무관. ① 친환경 제품보다 더 저렴한 제품을 선호한다 ② 심각한 개인적 희생을 요구하는 장기적인 변화에 전념한다 ③ 새로운 기술이 곧 모든 환경 문제를 해결하리라고 기대한다 ④ 고장 난 가정용품을 짧은 시간에 수리하는 도구에 의존한다 ⑤ 큰 실질적 변화를 요구하지 않고 죄책감을 빨리 덜어 주는 간단한 행동을 신뢰한다
choice.body: People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance. In their search for such a balance, people are inclined to believe in “quick-fixes,” because they want to re-establish the moral balance and escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible. In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their evaluation of past environmentally burdening behaviors and future environmentally friendly behaviors.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) relocating — (B) fixed homes — (C) shrinking
(A) isolated — (B) constant motion — (C) shrinking
(A) relocating — (B) constant motion — (C) expanding

order.A: People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance. order.B: Moral licensing has also been observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment. When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of “eco-guilt.”

order.D: Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing “eco-friendly” products, probably because they feel licensed to do so since they morally account the “eco-friendly” choice as a “good” deed.

para.en: Capitalism is not a system where cash is everywhere but rather one in which islands of cash exchange exist within oceans of cheap — or potentially cheap — natures. Reproducing life within the cash nexus is expensive, and it grows more expensive over time. Workers’ wages can be frozen, even rolled back, but in the end inequality leads to crises of the kind we’ve recently seen bring about populist protests in the United States and the United Kingdom. Workers demand dignity, and their labor becomes expensive. Production processes burn through an island, and energy is no longer cheap. The climate changes, and crops can no longer grow as abundantly as they once did. Frontiers are so important in these processes because they offer places where the new cheap things can be seized — and the cheap work of humans and other natures can be forcefully taken.

Some people are more likely to cheat and steal after purchasing “eco-friendly” products, probably because they feel licensed to do so since they morally account the “eco-friendly” choice as a “good” deed. Moral licensing has also been observed in the context of cooperation for the good of the environment. When people are reminded of deeds they have done that they know were harmful to the environment, they might be left with a feeling of “eco-guilt.” People who experience eco-guilt seek pro-environmental actions to compensate for this guilt and restore balance. In their search for such a balance, people are inclined to believe in “quick-fixes,” because they want to re-establish the moral balance and escape the guilt as quickly and easily as possible. In the same way that people may change their attitudes to reduce inconsistencies between attitudes and behavior, people may also change their evaluation of past environmentally burdening behaviors and future environmentally friendly behaviors. For instance, people are more likely to sign a petition addressing environmental damage after viewing evidence of human-caused environmental damage.

Human geography is becoming unclear. As people find themselves regularly on the move, we are experiencing a phase shift like when matter transitions from solid to liquid to gas: molecules heat up and loosen from one another, vibrating more rapidly. One might even say that humans are becoming like particles in quantum physics, their velocity and location always in flux. It would be nice to return to some form of stability, but that’s not how things work in a quantum world. Instead, the complexity of today’s world makes it increasingly difficult to settle permanently anywhere. Highly paid digital nomads and billionaires with multiple passports as well as migratory workers are all part of the diverse and growing global demographic of quantum people.

Of the cognitive motivations, the most fundamental one encourages people to understand their environment to predict what is going to happen in case of uncertainties. Most important, people prefer to develop meanings that are shared with other people. For example, if in a given year more people accept offers of admission than a college expects, quite a few students end up living in dorm lounges or campus hotels. It is easy to understand why living in the lounge is problematic (no closet, for one thing). But what is wrong with a room at campus hotels? After all, students in a hotel get private bathrooms, their own TV, and larger rooms. In fact, living in those hotels is problematic because the student residents are not a part of a stable group with people who will be their neighbors for the year; they must wait in uncertainty before finding their social niche. The uncertainty itself is the problem. People lack a shared social understanding, normally developed from membership in a stable group.

Psychological theories across the field agree on the importance of grieving our losses, from the highly personal through to the broadly collective. Grief is a dynamic emotional process essential to consciousness. At a psychological level, it supports us to both face into our own and others’ vulnerability, transience and mortality, and to repair life energy after significant loss. Grief work honours the loss, the sadness and the experience of diminishment or absence, while also setting up the ground for self-transformation and the continuation of life. Psychotherapist Fran Weller describes grief work is “an act of devotion, rooted in love and compassion” that requires “an ongoing practice of deepening, attending and listening.” When we grieve for what is lost, it clears the way towards a strengthening of love and commitment for what remains. In time this may build a desire to make good from the loss by repairing as many damages as we can and/or compensating for them. Grief can make us both very sad and very motivated to act.
